name: Rajendra Agarwal
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2022-2025); Forbes annual (2020-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2025); Hurun India (2017-2021)
forbes_bio: Medical doctor, whose family owned a pharmacy in Jaipur, set up Macleods Pharmaceuticals with his two brothers in 1986 to make anti-TB medicines.
Privately held Macleods Pharmaceuticals is among India's top 10 pharma firms.
Macleods produces generics for a range of diseases including asthma, osteoporosis and diabetes.
Agarwal's older brothers, Girdharilal Bawri and Banwarilal Bawri. who are also billionaires, are chairman and joint managing director respectively.
forbes_facts: Agarwal and his two brothers live together with their families in the same building in Mumbai.
The company was named after John Macleod, a Scottish doctor and author of medical textbooks.

name: Ralph Winterhalter
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026)
forbes_bio: Ralph Winterhalter owns Winterhalter, a family-owned maker of commercial dishwashers based in Meckenbeuren, Germany.
Winterhalter was founded by Karl Winterhalter in 1947, and is now controlled by his grandson Ralph Winterhalter, who owns the majority stake, and son Jurgen, the CEO.
Winterhalter has 2,000 employees and revenue of 475 million euros in 2024.
The company blog features articles on Oktoberfest beer mug hygiene, avoiding glass corrosion and how to properly place glasses on a dining table.

name: Erik Paulsson
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2017-2022); Hurun Global (2018-2025)
forbes_bio: In 1957, Erik Paulsson, then 17, and his younger brother Mats founded a waste management company to service the local farmers in the south of Sweden.
The company, later named PEAB, expanded to construction in 1970, the industry it's known for today.
While Mats and his family still control the company, Erik has divested into spin-offs of several PEAB property management entities.
His most valuable holdings are Fabege, Catena and Wihlborgs Fastigheter, all real estate companies traded on the Stockholm stock exchange.
In 2018, Paulsson retired from all board seats of the public companies in his portfolio but remains chairman of his investment entity, Backahill AB.
forbes_facts: In deciding who would get what in the division of PEAB, Paulsson and his brother reportedly flipped a coin.
Paulsson was charged for bribery after winning the contract to build Sweden's new 65,000 seat national football arena in 2011. The court cleared him of all charges.

name: Howard Huang
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026)
forbes_bio: Howard Huang is the founder, chairman and CEO of Orbbec, a developer of 3D vision cameras.
Its cameras allow machines to perceive depth like human eyes do, and enable them to better navigate the environment.
Backed by Chinese fintech giant Ant Group, the Shenzhen-based company supplies to Alipay for its facial recognition payment system.
It also sells to the robotics clients including Chinese service bot maker Pudu Robotics as well as humanoid developers such as state-backed X-Humanoid and Ant Group's Ant Lingbo Technology.
Huang took Orbbec public on Shanghai's Star market in a 1.2 billion yuan ($169 million) IPO in 2022.
forbes_facts: A trained engineer specializing in optical measurement, Huang founded Orbbec in 2013, hoping to turn his academic research into real-world applications.

name: José Neves
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2021); Hurun Global (2021-2022)
forbes_bio: Neves is founder and CEO of UK-based online luxury fashion platform Farfetch.
Farfetch went public on the New York Stock Exchange in September 2018.
Due to the company's dual-class stock structure, Neves owns less than 15% of the company's equity but has more than 77% of the voting rights.
Although he started as a programmer, Neves has worked as a shoe designer, boutique owner and trade show organizer.
forbes_facts: Neves started coding at the age of eight.
He sat on the British Fashion Council board from 2016 to 2018.

name: Liang Yunchao
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2013-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2011-2026)
forbes_bio: Liang Yunchao chairs Guandong By-health, one of China's largest producers of vitamins and health supplements.
Every few years he invites young leaders to join a "wildlife training" boot camp to test their stamina, he told Forbes Asia in an interview.
His favorite boot camp spots include Teklimakan Qumluqi in Xinjiang, the world's second largest desert, and Antarctica.

name: John MacMillan
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026)
forbes_bio: John MacMillan is one of 21 billionaire heirs to Cargill, the world's biggest agriculture business.
His great-great-grandfather, W.W. Cargill, founded the business as a single grain warehouse on the end of an Iowa railroad line in 1865.
The family still owns roughly 90% of Cargill, which did $154 billion in 2025 sales across food, agriculture, financial and industrial divisions.
The Cargill-MacMillan family collects an estimated 18% of net profits as dividends every year.

name: Ryu Kwang-ji

forbes_bio: Ryu Kwang-ji is CEO and the largest shareholder of Kumyang, a chemical company based in the South Korean port city of Busan.

Since 2022, Kumyang has been trying to expand into batteries for electric vehicles and hydrogen-fueled cars.
Ryu joined Kumyang in 1998 and took over as CEO three years later.
